warnings.problem: plan.version is still 1 and plan.history[] is empty, although this is the second plan body for this build (inputs/plan/plan-body.json then inputs/plan/plan-body-v2.json, 20 steps then 22) and the first was rejected at G2. standards/build-orchestration.md section 3 says 'Re-planning after a rejected gate is a new plan version (plan.version + 1); earlier versions stay in plan.history[]'. requirement.summary: Requester: Acme Software, B2B support team. Today support runs from a shared mailbox.

clarifications.question: Which picklist values differ between the support and finance case processes, field by field?
clarifications.why: If nothing differs, the requirement is a layout or Dynamic Forms problem, not a record type.
clarifications.answer_shape: The picklistValues blocks per record type, plus the evidence that a record type is warranted at all.
clarifications.proposed_default: Two Case record types (Support, Billing) differing on Status/Reason; if only the reply address and queue differ, use one record type plus Origin-driven routing instead.
clarifications.answer: Two Case record types (Support, Billing) differing on Status/Reason; if only the reply address and queue differ, use one record type plus Origin-driven routing instead. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Is this object Lead, Opportunity, Solution, or Case?
clarifications.why: Those four require a businessProcess; every other object forbids one, and both mistakes are deploy failures.
clarifications.answer_shape: The object name, and whether a BusinessProcess file must ship with the record type.
clarifications.proposed_default: Case — so a Support Process must be authored and deployed alongside every Case record type.
clarifications.answer: Case. The requirement is written entirely in terms of Case creation, case numbers and case ownership ("Within the first minute of a case being created..."), so a Support Process (BusinessProcess) must be authored and deployed alongside every Case record type.

clarifications.question: Which profile does each affected user actually hold?
clarifications.why: Permission sets grant record-type visibility only; the default record type and the page layout assignment exist solely on Profile.
clarifications.answer_shape: The profile x record type x layout matrix, not a per-record-type layout list.
clarifications.proposed_default: Three profiles matching the three teams (Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing), each with an explicit default record type and layout assignment.
clarifications.answer: Three profiles matching the three teams (Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing), each with an explicit default record type and layout assignment. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Do Cases already exist on any record type we are creating or retiring?
clarifications.why: Reassignment blanks any picklist value absent from the target record type, silently.
clarifications.answer_shape: The at-risk record count and the value-mapping step that must run first (zero is a valid answer, but it must be stated).
clarifications.proposed_default: None — support runs from a shared mailbox today, so this is a greenfield Case model; confirm no legacy Cases exist in the org.
clarifications.answer: None. The requirement states support currently runs from a shared mailbox ("Today support runs from a shared mailbox"), so no Salesforce Case records exist yet on any record type — this is a greenfield Case model; still confirm no legacy Cases exist in the org before deploying record types.

clarifications.question: Is a field being marked Required on the layout meant to be enforced everywhere?
clarifications.why: Layout Required binds to that layout only — API, Flow, and every other layout ignore it.
clarifications.answer_shape: A decision between field-level required and a record-type-scoped validation rule, per field.
clarifications.proposed_default: Priority and Origin enforced at field or validation-rule level, because Web-to-Case and Email-to-Case create Cases through the API, not through a layout.
clarifications.answer: Priority and Origin enforced at field or validation-rule level, because Web-to-Case and Email-to-Case create Cases through the API, not through a layout. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Are Person Accounts enabled on this org?
clarifications.why: Person Account record types are a separate model, and the Metadata API will not round-trip their custom picklist values.
clarifications.answer_shape: Yes/no, plus a separate design track and a manual picklist verification step if yes.
clarifications.proposed_default: No — Acme is B2B, so Cases hang off Business Accounts and Contacts.
clarifications.answer: No. The requirement describes Acme as "Acme Software, B2B support team," so Cases hang off Business Accounts and Contacts, not Person Accounts.

clarifications.question: What is on the current profile that has no permission-set equivalent?
clarifications.why: loginHours, loginIpRanges, layoutAssignments, the default app and the default record type exist only on Profile. They are the residue, and the only reason a profile still exists.
clarifications.answer_shape: The residue list — the exact contents of the base profile file.
clarifications.proposed_default: A minimal base profile per team carrying only layout assignments, default app and default record type; every object, field and tab grant lives in permission sets.
clarifications.answer: A minimal base profile per team carrying only layout assignments, default app and default record type; every object, field and tab grant lives in permission sets. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Which users hold this profile, and do they all hold the same user licence?
clarifications.why: A permission set with a LicenseId can only be assigned where the profile's UserLicenseId matches; a mixed-licence population must be split before, not after.
clarifications.answer_shape: The population split by licence, and whether LicenseId should be left empty.
clarifications.proposed_default: 18 internal users (12 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 2 Billing) on Salesforce licences with Service Cloud; leave LicenseId empty on the permission sets.
clarifications.answer: 18 internal users split 12 Tier 1 / 4 Tier 2 / 2 Billing (per requirement's team counts), all on Salesforce licences with Service Cloud (per requirement: "We are moving to Service Cloud"); leave LicenseId empty on the permission sets (default accepted for that design decision — dry run).

clarifications.question: Which objects, fields, tabs, apps, record types, layouts and classes are in scope?
clarifications.why: A profile retrieve returns permissions only for what else is in the same manifest. Without this list the retrieved profile is silently incomplete.
clarifications.answer_shape: The package.xml that makes the retrieve honest, reused for the deploy.
clarifications.proposed_default: Case, Account, Contact, EmailMessage, Entitlement, plus the Case record types, layouts and the Service app.
clarifications.answer: Case, Account, Contact, EmailMessage, Entitlement, plus the Case record types, layouts and the Service app. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Are we adding access, or taking it away?
clarifications.why: Permission sets only grant. Removing access means editing the profile explicitly to false, or muting inside a group — two mechanisms with different blast radii.
clarifications.answer_shape: Additive or strip, and which mechanism applies.
clarifications.proposed_default: Additive — this is a new Service Cloud footprint, so every grant is new and no strip phase is required.
clarifications.answer: Additive — this is a new Service Cloud footprint, so every grant is new and no strip phase is required. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Is the profile standard (custom=false) or custom?
clarifications.why: Editing standard objects on standard profiles is disabled in API 50.0+, so the strip phase will not apply.
clarifications.answer_shape: A clone-first decision, recorded before any deploy is attempted.
clarifications.proposed_default: Clone Standard User into custom profiles before any deploy is attempted.
clarifications.answer: Clone Standard User into custom profiles before any deploy is attempted. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Who exactly does this work — an employee, a customer, a partner, or a contractor?
clarifications.why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation, object access and portal template long before design starts.
clarifications.answer_shape: A licence_implication value, and an escalation to architect/license-optimization-strategy if the answer is not an employee.
clarifications.proposed_default: Employees only — 18 internal support and finance staff; the customer portal is explicitly out of scope for this phase.
clarifications.answer: Employees only. The requirement describes the work as done entirely by internal Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Billing staff (18 people total), and explicitly lists "customer portal" as out of scope for this phase.

clarifications.question: When you say only Finance sees billing cases — can others not open the record at all, or can they open it but should not see a field on it?
clarifications.why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms configured in different places; record access itself is seven ordered layers.
clarifications.answer_shape: A sharing_impact value naming the layer — OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rule, team, manual/Apex, restriction — plus a separate FLS row.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: What must NOT happen automatically, and who fixes it when the automation is wrong?
clarifications.why: "Make it automatic" hides the trigger, the condition, the exception path and the owner of the failure.
clarifications.answer_shape: The exception path and a named owner, which is what makes the automation row estimable.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Which channels create cases, at what steady-state volume, and what is the biggest single batch anyone would ever push?
clarifications.why: Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case and manual entry have different limits, routing behaviour and spam exposure; and automation that passes UAT on ten records fails on a bulk load, because Flow and Apex share the transaction limits.
clarifications.answer_shape: A channel inventory with the daily limit and pending-queue risk for each, plus a steady-state number and a worst-case batch number.
clarifications.proposed_default: Email-to-Case ~400/day (support@ and billing@), Web-to-Case ~60/day, manual ~20/day, no phone; no bulk Case load is planned, so the worst-case batch is the daily email peak.
clarifications.answer: Email-to-Case ~400/day (support@acme.example and billing@acme.example combined), Web-to-Case ~60/day, manual agent entry ~20/day, no phone channel (per requirement). No bulk Case load is planned, so the worst-case batch is the daily email peak (~400).

clarifications.question: What must happen in the first minute: owner, acknowledgement, calendar, priority?
clarifications.why: Assignment, auto-response, business hours and priority all resolve during the save; anything set later runs on the wrong clock.
clarifications.answer_shape: The before-save Flow scope and the assignment-rule design, stated as an ordered list of what happens during the save.
clarifications.proposed_default: All four in the first minute: assignment rule sets the owner, auto-response sends the acknowledgement with the case number, a before-save Flow stamps Case.BusinessHoursId, and priority is mapped from the form field or the mailbox.
clarifications.answer: All four in the first minute, per requirement: an owner is assigned, the customer receives an acknowledgement with the case number, the SLA clock is running on the right calendar, and priority is set from what the form or email tells us.

clarifications.question: Which public addresses do customers actually write to, and does the same mailbox forward to more than one place?
clarifications.why: Each address is one routingAddresses element; a mailbox that forwards twice duplicates every case, and two elements sharing an emailAddress have no deterministic configuration.
clarifications.answer_shape: The channel list with one forwarding rule each, checked by the duplicate-address ERROR in the skill's checker.
clarifications.proposed_default: Two routing addresses: support@acme.example and billing@acme.example, each forwarding to exactly one Salesforce routing address.
clarifications.answer: Two addresses: support@acme.example and billing@acme.example (per requirement). Per the answer key, IT owns the forwarding rules for both mailboxes. Per the proposed default, assume each forwards to exactly one Salesforce routing address (default accepted — dry run for that specific claim); confirm with IT before go-live that neither mailbox has a second forwarding rule.

clarifications.question: Which queue owns each channel's cases?
clarifications.why: caseOwner on a routing address writes the org-level defaultCaseOwner, so a second address setting it overwrites the first.
clarifications.answer_shape: Ownership expressed as caseOrigin per address plus assignment rule entries, not as caseOwner.
clarifications.proposed_default: Express ownership as caseOrigin per address plus assignment-rule entries: support@ -> Tier 1 queue, billing@ -> Billing queue; leave caseOwner unset on both addresses.
clarifications.answer: support@acme.example routes to Tier 1 (general support); billing@acme.example routes to the Billing/Finance queue — per requirement: "Finance queries arrive at billing@acme.example and should be worked by Finance." Express ownership as caseOrigin per address plus assignment-rule entries; leave caseOwner unset on both addresses (default accepted for that technical mechanism — dry run).

clarifications.question: Is the Case.Origin picklist value for each channel already active in the org?
clarifications.why: caseOrigin is the only per-address value an assignment rule can read; a value not in the picklist stamps something nobody can filter on.
clarifications.answer_shape: The picklist additions that must deploy before or with the settings file.
clarifications.proposed_default: Add Email-Support, Email-Billing and Web as active Case.Origin values, deployed before or with the Case settings file.
clarifications.answer: Add Email-Support, Email-Billing and Web as active Case.Origin values, deployed before or with the Case settings file. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Is this org on Lightning Threading or legacy threading?
clarifications.why: Two mutually exclusive pairs of token switches exist and the wrong pair is inert.
clarifications.answer_shape: The one pair of threading switches to set, plus useEmailHeadersForThreading as the gateway fallback.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: What should happen to mail we refuse — bounce it or drop it?

clarifications.answer_shape: A class scoped to what that user can actually reach, plus a manual fallback for what it cannot.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Which settings, endpoints and credentials must never point at production after a copy?
clarifications.why: Integration endpoints and scheduled jobs survive a refresh still aimed at live systems.
clarifications.answer_shape: The seed values the post-copy class writes, per environment.
clarifications.proposed_default: The Email-to-Case routing addresses and the website form endpoint must be re-pointed on every refresh, or the sandbox will answer real customer mail.
clarifications.answer: The Email-to-Case routing addresses and the website form endpoint must be re-pointed on every refresh, or the sandbox will answer real customer mail. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Which sandbox is UAT in, when was it last refreshed, and is another refresh booked inside the window?
clarifications.why: A refresh during UAT deletes the build and the seeded data; a Full sandbox's 29-day floor makes teams book refreshes far in advance and forget them.
clarifications.answer_shape: refreshed_on and build_deployed_on in the plan header, plus a named person who can veto a refresh.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Does any acceptance criterion depend on data volume — a rollup, a queue backlog, a query, a batch?
clarifications.why: A Partial Copy holds a sample, so volume-dependent behaviour cannot be proved in it.
clarifications.answer_shape: The sandbox type decision, and an explicit list of cases the chosen environment cannot prove.
clarifications.proposed_default: Yes — 400 emails a day against the Email-to-Case daily limit and the Tier 1 queue backlog; list the cases the chosen sandbox type cannot prove.
clarifications.answer: Yes — per requirement, ~400 emails/day arrive at support@/billing@, a volume the Email-to-Case daily limit and Tier 1 queue backlog behaviour depend on; list the cases the chosen sandbox type (e.g. Partial Copy) cannot prove (default accepted for the sandbox-type framing — dry run).

clarifications.question: Which named user, with which profile and permission sets, runs each test case?
clarifications.why: An admin bypasses FLS and most sharing in the UI, so an admin pass proves nothing about the persona.
clarifications.answer_shape: A persona table with real usernames — the roster the sign-off record is anchored to.
clarifications.proposed_default: One named tester per team — Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing — on the real profile and permission sets, never the admin.
clarifications.answer: One named tester per team — Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing (matching the requirement's team structure) — on the real profile and permission sets, never the admin. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Does any criterion involve an email arriving, and who has to receive it?
clarifications.why: Sandboxes default to System Email Only, and only User.Email is .invalid-suffixed on refresh — Contact and Lead emails are real.
clarifications.answer_shape: A deliverability setting recorded with a date, and scrubbed contact emails before it is raised.
clarifications.proposed_default: Yes — the acknowledgement is a core promise, so raise deliverability deliberately and scrub Contact emails before doing so.
clarifications.answer: Yes — the acknowledgement is a core promise, so raise deliverability deliberately and scrub Contact emails before doing so. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: How will test data be created — UI, Data Loader, Bulk API, REST?
clarifications.why: The three load paths disagree about whether assignment rules run at all.
clarifications.answer_shape: The tool and its assignment-rule setting written into the case preconditions, with a UI control record to compare against.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Which criteria are restrictions rather than capabilities — what must be blocked, hidden, or rejected?
clarifications.why: A script built only from "the user can..." never touches a validation rule, FLS or sharing.
clarifications.answer_shape: At least one negative_path case per story, and a go decision that is invalid without them.
clarifications.proposed_default: At minimum: Tier 1 must not see billing cases if that is the intent, and an unauthorised sender's mail must bounce rather than create a case.
clarifications.answer: At minimum: Tier 1 must not see billing cases if that is the intent, and an unauthorised sender's mail must bounce rather than create a case. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: For each expected result, what would the tester actually look at — a screen, a query, a mailbox, a file?
clarifications.why: The oracle decides the evidence type and the automation verdict; a then clause with no observable is not testable.
clarifications.answer_shape: An evidence entry per case and an automation_candidate of apex, flow-test or none.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: For every deny case: what is the persona set up without, and is anything else already blocking it?
clarifications.why: A permission set can grant but never deny, and a scoping rule empties a list view without removing access.
clarifications.answer_shape: A deny that is attributable to a named mechanism rather than to a coincidence.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Which UI does each persona actually use — Lightning desktop, the mobile app, or Classic?
clarifications.why: formFactor is what selects the override the persona sees, and the three values are different pages.
clarifications.answer_shape: A precondition per case naming the form factor, with steps runnable by the person assigned them.
clarifications.proposed_default: Lightning desktop for all three teams; no mobile requirement is stated in this phase.
clarifications.answer: Lightning desktop for all three teams; no mobile requirement is stated in this phase. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Is the expected result reachable through the path the persona uses, or only through the one the admin used?
clarifications.why: UI-created records and API-loaded records go through different halves of the save order; layout-level rules run for one and not the other.
clarifications.answer_shape: A separate case per load path, not one case that quietly proves the easier half.
clarifications.proposed_default: Test each of the three intake channels separately — Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case and manual UI — rather than proving the easy half once.
clarifications.answer: Test each of the three intake channels separately — Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case and manual UI (matching the requirement's three channels) — rather than proving the easy half once. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Which reports, list views, and Flow entry criteria filter on this record type today?
clarifications.why: Report filters key on the label, which is not stable; code and Flows key on DeveloperName, which is.
clarifications.answer_shape: The rename blast radius, enumerated before anyone renames anything.
clarifications.proposed_default: None today; fix DeveloperName values now so the later rename blast radius is zero.
clarifications.answer: None today; fix DeveloperName values now so the later rename blast radius is zero. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Does a managed package require this profile to be assigned?
clarifications.why: Some packages ship profile-dependent configuration that a permission set cannot replace.
clarifications.answer_shape: A documented exception list, or confirmation that the package ships its own permission sets.
clarifications.proposed_default: None known; confirm against the org's installed-package list before the access step runs.
clarifications.answer: None known; confirm against the org's installed-package list before the access step runs. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Who verifies access afterwards, and against what?
clarifications.why: "It deployed" is not evidence. Effective access is the union of the profile and every assigned permission set, visible per user in Setup.
clarifications.answer_shape: A named verification step: a View Summary check plus the assignment-count SOQL.
clarifications.proposed_default: The CRM admin lead runs a View Summary check on one user per team plus the assignment-count query, before UAT opens.
clarifications.answer: The CRM admin lead runs a View Summary check on one user per team plus the assignment-count query, before UAT opens. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Who should be notified of a new record: shared mailbox, every member, nobody?
clarifications.why: email and doesSendEmailToMembers are independent switches.
clarifications.answer_shape: Per queue: the notification address, and whether member email is on.
clarifications.proposed_default: A shared mailbox per queue rather than every member, so notifications are read rather than filtered.
clarifications.answer: Per the answer key: Tier 1 uses Omni-Channel push, so no queue email; Billing wants the queue address emailed. Tier 2 is not addressed by the answer key — for Tier 2, apply the proposed default of a shared mailbox per queue rather than every member (default accepted for the Tier 2 portion — dry run).

clarifications.question: What happens to queue-owned records when a queue is retired?
clarifications.why: Records owned by a retired queue are stranded.
clarifications.answer_shape: A retirement step in the runbook, with the reassignment target named.
clarifications.proposed_default: A retirement step in the runbook: reassign open Cases to the surviving queue before the queue is deleted.
clarifications.answer: A retirement step in the runbook: reassign open Cases to the surviving queue before the queue is deleted. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Who maintains next year's holidays, and when?
clarifications.why: Holidays expire; unmaintained calendars silently stop pausing.
clarifications.answer_shape: An owner and a yearly deploy slot in the release calendar.
clarifications.proposed_default: A named owner in Service Operations, with a yearly holiday deploy booked in the release calendar each Q4.
clarifications.answer: A named owner in Service Operations, with a yearly holiday deploy booked in the release calendar each Q4. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: How will we know next month that the escalation rule still fires?
clarifications.why: IsEscalated is a plain writable boolean, not an engine-owned lock — nothing reports on a rule that quietly stopped.
clarifications.answer_shape: A saved report or query on escalated, still-open cases, with an owner and a cadence.
clarifications.proposed_default: A saved report on escalated, still-open Cases, reviewed weekly by the Tier 2 lead.
clarifications.answer: A saved report on escalated, still-open Cases, reviewed weekly by the Tier 2 lead. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Is entitlement versioning on, and who owns the next version?
clarifications.why: The version fields do nothing until the org switch is on, and an SLA change means a new file with every time-trigger offset re-derived.
clarifications.answer_shape: The versioning switch state and a named owner for version bumps.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Does each message fit in 255 characters and name both the problem and the fix?
clarifications.why: errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that cannot say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence.
clarifications.answer_shape: The final message text per rule, under 255 characters, naming both the problem and the fix.
clarifications.proposed_default: Write the final message text at design time, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time.
clarifications.answer: Write the final message text at design time, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: Who owns each environment, and who approves its refresh?
clarifications.why: An environment with no owner is the one that gets refreshed over someone's uncommitted work.
clarifications.answer_shape: A named owner per environment, and a separate named approver for its refresh.
clarifications.proposed_default: A named owner per row of the topology table, with the data owner (not the refresher) accountable for approving a refresh.
clarifications.answer: A named owner per row of the topology table, with the data owner (not the refresher) accountable for approving a refresh. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: When must the validation deploy run relative to sign-off, and who accepts a deferred defect?
clarifications.why: A quick deploy only skips tests within 10 days of a successful validation, so a validation taken at the start of a three-week cycle is dead by sign-off.
clarifications.answer_shape: A dated validation slot in the plan, and a named business owner for the known-issues list.
clarifications.answer: DEFER: not decidable in the dry run — planner to assume the conservative option and record an assumption

clarifications.question: Which permission set or group carries the feature, and is its recalculation finished?
clarifications.why: PermissionSetGroup.Status is a real picklist — Outdated or Updating means the tester does not yet have what the script assumes.
clarifications.answer_shape: A pre-run gate query, and the PSG each persona depends on.
clarifications.proposed_default: A pre-run gate query on PermissionSetGroup.Status before each UAT session, so a false-fail is not logged as a build defect.
clarifications.answer: A pre-run gate query on PermissionSetGroup.Status before each UAT session, so a false-fail is not logged as a build defect. (default accepted — dry run)

clarifications.question: When a test case fails, who decides Fail versus Blocked?
clarifications.why: Blocked is an environment result and must not raise a defect against the build; conflating them corrupts the defect data.
clarifications.answer_shape: A named triager and a re-runnable run sheet.
clarifications.proposed_default: A named triager (the QA or BA lead) with a run sheet whose rows are re-runnable rather than overwritten.
clarifications.answer: A named triager (the QA or BA lead) with a run sheet whose rows are re-runnable rather than overwritten. (default accepted — dry run)

assumptions.because: Q33 was deferred and no skill supplies a defensible default; no cited skill documents a default for it, so the step takes the blocked exit (build-planner Step 6) instead of a guess.

assumptions.because: Q35 was deferred; no cited skill documents a default for it, so the step takes the blocked exit (build-planner Step 6) instead of a guess.

assumptions.text: No report or code needs elapsed working time, so no working-time field is built in this phase.

assumptions.text: Every validation rule fires on a field the user edits on the Case itself; no rule reaches into a child record.

assumptions.text: No automation writes the fields the validation rules guard after save; the before-save stamping flow is the only writer and it runs before validation.
assumptions.because: Q55 was deferred; this is consistent with D1 and with Q27's single-owner-writer answer, and it is the assumption the artefacts must be checked against. (source: deferred clarification Q55)

assumptions.text: Every field a validation rule attaches its error to is present on both Case layouts.

M1-S02's checker does not prove it at step scope — it sees layouts and no record types — so the assertion sits in M1-S02's manual test and in M1's milestone checker at --manifest-dir artefacts.

assumptions.text: The only reporting requirement in this phase is the escalation monitoring report Q91 names.

assumptions.text: For every deny case, the persona is set up without the granting permission set and nothing else is already blocking the path.

assumptions.text: The as-is process is the shared mailbox described in the requirement and nothing more; no as-is map is produced.
assumptions.because: Q67 was deferred; the requirement's own first line is the only as-is evidence available. (source: deferred clarification Q67)

assumptions.text: One sandbox is available for the proof and its refresh is not contended.
assumptions.because: Q69 was deferred; the plan needs exactly one environment and assumes no more than that. (source: deferred clarification Q69)

assumptions.text: No environment in the ladder has a refresh floor that blocks the proof window.

assumptions.text: Test data is created through the UI by the named testers, not by a bulk load.

assumptions.text: Each expected result is evidenced by a screen the tester can point at, plus the case record itself; no query or file evidence is designed in this phase.

assumptions.text: Entitlement versioning is off and no next version is owned.

assumptions.text: Case carries exactly two record types, Support and Billing — the conditional in Q1's answer ('if only the reply address and queue differ, use one record type') is resolved in favour of two.

RecordTypeId is that field, so a single record type would leave no record-level criterion to keep Billing cases away from Tier 1 (assumption A1).

assumptions.text: One MilestoneType ('First Response') serves both tiers, and the differing 4-business-hour / 1-business-day targets live as minutesToComplete on two EntitlementProcess files. The count is therefore two entitlement processes and one milestone type.

Recorded as a documented skill default, not a guess.

assumptions.text: The two Case Support Processes select from the CaseStatus value set as it already stands; no new Status value is added and no StandardValueSet:CaseStatus file is deployed.

Recorded as an assumption rather than a fact because the answer enumerates no values. admin/case-management-setup/references/metadata-examples.md § 2 makes the dependency explicit ('The process is a subset of the CaseStatus values deployed in §1, so §1 lands first'), so if the builder finds a required Status value missing, M1-S01 blocks rather than inventing one.

decisions.decision: Stamp Case.EntitlementId, Case.BusinessHoursId and the Priority default in one before-save record-triggered Flow rather than in Apex or an after-save Flow.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q2. Does the logic run in under ~10s and touch only fields on the record itself?
    ├── Yes, but the field is OwnerId (or an acknowledgement, or an SLA
    │        clock) on a Case or a Lead                               → Q13
    ├── Yes  → Before-save record-triggered Flow
    └── No   → Q3
decisions.rationale: All three writes land on the triggering Case and the Account/Entitlement reads are lookups, not DML, so Q1's record-change branch reaches Q2. Q2's first branch redirects the Case-specific engine choices to Q13, and this plan takes that redirect elsewhere: the owner write is D3 (Q13), the acknowledgement is the auto-response rule in M3-S04 (Q13), and the SLA engine itself is the entitlement process in M4-S02 (Q15). What is left at Q2's plain 'Yes' leaf is exactly this step — the same-record field write that puts the Case into that engine. The Q15 leaf note is why the step has to exist at all: 'neither Email-to-Case nor Web-to-Case supplies an entitlement, so a case-intake design that stops at the channel tracks nothing until something assigns one.'
alternatives_rejected: three separate flows, one per field
decisions.consequences: No Apex means no coverage gate and no deploy-time test dependency, but also no custom exception handling: a Case whose Account has no entitlement must fall through to a documented default rather than throw (Q48).

decisions.decision: The stamping flow is before-save, not after-save: the Account and Entitlement lookups are read-only Get Records, which a before-save flow supports.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q3. Do you need any DML, an Action/callout, or an email — anything beyond
    writing fields on the triggering record?
    ├── No   → Before-Save record-triggered flow. Its element set is
                Assignment, Decision, Get Records, Loop — so a read-only
                cross-object lookup is fine here; a write is not.
decisions.rationale: Q1 'record INSERT or UPDATE' → Q2 'only set fields on the SAME record' → Q3 'no DML, no action, no email' → before-save. The branch text settles the one thing that looked like an obstacle: the cross-object read is allowed.
decisions.consequences: The customer acknowledgement (an email) cannot live in this flow; it stays in the auto-response rule (M3-S04), which is what Q63 asked for anyway.

decisions.decision: Case ownership at creation is set by Case Assignment Rules, and the assignment rule is the sole authoritative OwnerId writer at create time.
decisions.rationale: automation-selection Q2's first branch redirects an OwnerId write on a Case to Q13, and Q13's first leaf is this decision verbatim: the first owner is a function of field values (Origin, Account support tier) held in an ordered criteria table. The tree's own 'Why each leaf' note adds the reason a Flow is wrong here: assignment rules run at save-order position 9, after all after triggers and before after-save record-triggered flows at position 14, so a before-save Flow that sets OwnerId is simply overwritten. skills/admin/assignment-rules/references/routing-selector.md row 1 says the same thing and is recorded as the corroborating source.
alternatives_rejected: Omni-Channel alone with no queue-landing rule
decisions.consequences: Two by-design post-save OwnerId writers remain (Omni-Channel push in M3-S05 and the escalation rule in M4-S04). Q27 already flagged this; owner-writer-map.md in M3-S04 is the artefact that has to reconcile all three.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q13. Which native rule engine on Case or Lead owns this write?
     ├── The first owner comes from an ordered criteria table
     │   of field values                                          → Assignment Rules · `admin/assignment-rules`

decisions.decision: Tier 1 receives pushed work through queue-based Omni-Channel granted by profile; Tier 2 and Billing pull from queue list views.
decisions.rationale: Q13's second leaf is the decision: the question is who is free, not which team, and the tree's 'Why each leaf' note states that Omni-Channel sits on top of the assignment rule rather than instead of it — the rule lands the Case in the queue, Omni-Channel pushes it to an agent. That settles the mechanism. It does not settle the configuration: Q32-Q35 (objects pushed and capacity release, capacity model and weight, routing model and tie-breaker, push timeout) were all deferred at G1 and no cited skill documents a default for three of the four, so M3-S05 is written blocked rather than carrying invented numbers.
alternatives_rejected: Skills-based routing (Q37: no skill dimension in the requirement)
Per-user presence assignment (Q36: Tier 1 membership changes monthly)
decisions.consequences: Omni-Channel writes OwnerId after save, which is the second of the three owner writers D3 has to reconcile. M3-S05 is blocked on Q32-Q35, so nothing in this build configures the push half; Tier 1 works the Tier 1 General queue list view produced by M5-S01 until those four questions are answered.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q13. Which native rule engine on Case or Lead owns this write?
     ├── The record is already in a queue and must reach whichever
     │   agent is online and under capacity                       → Omni-Channel · `admin/omni-channel-routing-setup`

decisions.decision: Case org-wide default stays Private and Tier 2 reaches Support cases through a criteria-based sharing rule on record type; nothing extends Billing cases to Tier 1.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q3. Can the access be described by "anyone who matches criteria X should see records matching criteria Y"?
    ├── Yes, criteria are on the record itself          → Criteria-Based Sharing Rule
decisions.rationale: Q1 'Private → Q2'; the three teams are peers, not a hierarchy, so Q2's 'No' branch leads to Q3; the access is exactly 'the Tier 2 group should see cases whose RecordType is Support', and RecordTypeId is on the record itself.
decisions.consequences: Deferred Q13 asked whether the Billing restriction is record-level or field-level. The plan takes the record-level (more restrictive) reading as assumption A1. If the answer turns out to be field-level masking, M2-S05 is re-planned, not patched.

decisions.decision: The website form posts to native Web-to-Case; no middleware, no Bulk API and no custom REST endpoint is introduced.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q14. Which intake channel creates the Case?
     ├── Customer email to a monitored routing address            → Email-to-Case · `admin/email-to-case-configuration`
     ├── An HTML form posted from a public website                → Web-to-Case · `admin/case-management-setup`
decisions.rationale: Q13's fourth leaf ('The record arrives from an inbound intake channel') routes to Q14, whose second leaf is native Web-to-Case for an HTML form posted from a public website and whose first is Email-to-Case for a monitored routing address. That is the positive half of this decision, and it is what the v1 plan was missing. integration-pattern-selection Q5 was also read and settles the negative half by volume: 60 web submissions plus 400 emails a day sit in its lowest band, so Bulk API 2.0 and an iPaaS are ruled out. The tree's Q14 'Why each leaf' note adds the constraint the plan follows in M3-S03 and M3-S04: ownership belongs in the assignment rule reading Case.Origin per address, not in the channel's own owner field.
decisions.consequences: Q66 left open whether the form posts directly or through middleware. If middleware turns out to sit in front, the Origin stamping in M3-S03 and the assignment criteria in M3-S04 both change. Assumption A26 is not recorded because Q66 is answered — the answer itself says 'confirm', so the confirmation is a manual test on M3-S03.

decisions.decision: The 8-business-hour Tier 2 handoff is a Case Escalation Rule, not a scheduled Flow or a time-based Apex job.
decisions.rationale: Q13's fifth leaf ('Something must happen because time has passed') routes to Q15, whose first leaf is this decision: re-route or notify when an open Case ages past a threshold. The tree's 'Why each leaf' note is the reason a scheduled Flow is wrong: escalation rules run at save-order position 12 and then on their own timer against business hours, and a polling Flow 'will not honour the per-entry businessHoursSource or the escalationStartTime choice between case creation and last modification' — both of which Q42 and Q43 answered explicitly. automation-selection Q10 and async-selection were both read and route only between Batch, Queueable and Schedule-triggered Flow, all of which re-implement the engine.
alternatives_rejected: After-save Flow with a scheduled path
decisions.consequences: The escalation engine batches, so the 480-minute threshold is not a to-the-second promise (Q46 asked for headroom to be agreed). The rule also writes OwnerId, which is the third owner writer D3 has to reconcile.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q15. What does the passage of time have to do?
     ├── Re-route or notify when an open Case ages past a
     │   threshold                                                → Escalation Rules · `admin/escalation-rules`

decisions.decision: Nothing in this build runs asynchronously: no @future, no Queueable, no Batch, no Schedulable and no Platform Event.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q1. How many records / how long?
    ├── < 2,000 records, < 60s          → Q2
    ├── 2k – 50k, < 5 min                → Q5 (Queueable)
    ├── > 50k OR > 5 min                 → Q8 (Batch Apex)
    └── Truly massive, one-off ETL       → Bulk API 2.0 (async SOQL / external job)
decisions.rationale: The worst case anyone described is the daily email peak of ~400 cases (Q15), and those arrive as individual API inserts, never as one 2,000-record transaction. Q1's first band applies and the tree never reaches an async tier.
decisions.consequences: Every automation in the plan runs inside the creating transaction, so the before-save flow in M4-S03 is on the critical path of every intake. If volume grows past the Q1 first band, this decision is the one to revisit.

decisions.decision: Case is treated as an ordinary object: no skinny table, no custom index request and no archival design in this phase.
decisions.branch_quote:
Q10. What stage of LDV are you in?
    ├── Designing a new high-volume object           → architect/large-data-volume-architecture (skinny + indexes from day one)
decisions.rationale: The tree was entered because the requirement names a volume (Q15: ~480 cases/day). Q1's symptom router has no branch for a greenfield design with no reported symptom, so Q10's design-stage branch is the only reachable entry. ~480/day is roughly 175k Cases a year, well below the thresholds that branch exists for, so the answer is 'not this'.
alternatives_rejected: Skinny table on Case from day one
Big Object archival of closed cases
decisions.consequences: The escalation monitoring report (M5-S01) and the queue list views (M5-S01) are unindexed selective queries today. Q76 already asked which acceptance criteria depend on volume; if the report degrades, this decision is where the revisit starts.

decisions.decision: Mark the First Response milestone complete with an after-update Apex trigger on Case that stamps CaseMilestone.CompletionDate, not with entitlement-process completion criteria and not with a Flow.
decisions.rationale: automation-selection was read end to end before this was called treeless. Q2's first branch sends an SLA clock on a Case to Q13, and Q13's fifth leaf sends it to Q15, whose second leaf selects Entitlement milestones as the engine — that is D-level ground for M4-S02 and nothing more; no leaf in Q13, Q14 or Q15 says who writes CompletionDate. Q3's Apex list does not name it either. The skill is the source: skills/admin/entitlements-and-milestones/references/gotchas.md gotcha 8 states that a milestone stays open until something writes CompletionDate and that the mechanism must ship with the process, and references/metadata-examples.md § 9 shows CaseMilestone supports only update() with CompletionDate and StartDate as its two updateable fields. skills/apex/entitlement-apex-hooks declares exactly this artefact as its output — an after-update trigger on Case that writes CompletionDate to open CaseMilestone records, plus its test class — so the Apex path is the one the library documents end to end. The declarative alternative is not chosen because no cited reference documents an EntitlementProcess completion-criteria element; milestoneCriteriaFilterItems is a start criterion (api_meta.txt:59198-59201), not a completion one.
alternatives_rejected: Satisfiable completion criteria on the entitlement process (no completion-criteria element is documented in the skill's metadata reference)

A record-triggered Flow stamping CompletionDate directly (metadata-examples § 9 documents the Flow path as an invocable wrapper around this same Apex, so it adds a component without removing the Apex)
Leaving completion manual (gotcha 8: every first-response milestone then reports violated on cases the agent demonstrably answered)
decisions.consequences: This is the only Apex in the build, so M4-S05 is the only step under the 75% coverage gate and the only one whose artefacts a deploy will compile. Violation polling is deliberately not built: the same skill's MilestoneViolationScheduler is Schedulable, which D8 rules out for this phase.

acceptance_tests.description: Every Case validation rule in the milestone parses, has no duplicate fullName across files, and carries an errorDisplayField that resolves. Note for the reader: this checker returns 1 on any finding including REVIEW, so the milestone passes only if the formulas keep the explicit ISBLANK( blank guard M3-S01's own test describes.

W01: the consumer half of M2-S01's custom-permission assertion, carried where it can actually be made. At artefacts/M2-S01 the checker sees the definition and the grant but no consumer, so 'Distinct permissions referenced' is 0 and a validation rule naming a non-existent permission cannot be seen. Over the whole tree, once M3-S01's rules exist, the same command printed 'Custom permissions defined: 1 / Permission sets / profiles parsed: 8 / Distinct permissions referenced: 1' and the coverage row 'Bypass_Case_Intake_Validation  2  permission set Case_Intake_Integration', exit 0. The same tree with one rule's $Permission reference changed to Bypass_Ghost printed one WARN and exited 0 plain, 1 under --strict — which is why --strict is declared: an unresolvable consumer reference is a WARN in this checker, and without --strict the exit code would not carry it.
Every settings file, rule set, template and Omni-Channel component in M3 appears in the milestone package.xml with a file behind it.

Given M3-S05 is blocked on deferred Q32-Q35, when the milestone gate is reached, then the support manager acknowledges that no Omni-Channel push is built in this phase, that Tier 1 works the Tier 1 General queue list view (M5-S01) in the interim, and that Q32-Q35 have a named owner and a due date.

Given check_case_management_setup.py is NOT declared as an M3 milestone test, when the M3 gate is reached, then the reviewer knows why: run at --manifest-dir artefacts with M3-S04's assignment rules in scope it reports 'No active case assignment rule found in metadata' on a correctly-active file, because it reads <active> as a direct child of <AssignmentRules> where the element never lives (it sits inside <assignmentRule>). The same checker IS declared on M3-S03, where no assignment rules are in scope and it exits 0. This is a deepen-a-skill signal for admin/case-management-setup, recorded rather than worked around.
